fixtures.canonicalText: At first light two boats were drawn up on the shingle below the village. Erran had been told, the winter before, that the far shore was empty. He did not believe it. The older of the two boats belonged to his uncle, who had not yet come to the water. Erran pushed the smaller boat out alone. Fog stood on the channel and the far shore was not visible. Someone on the shingle called after him, but the words did not carry. By the time the fog lifted he was past the middle of the channel. The far shore was not empty. He turned the boat and went back, and did not say what he had seen.

fixtures.canonicalText:
Tell me about a time you got lost. Take as long as you need.
Okay. Um. There was a market — this was maybe two years ago — and I went in through one entrance and I could not find the way back out.
Can you tell me anything more about that?
It was hot. There were stalls with fabric hanging down so you couldn't see over them.
Do you remember what time of day it was?
Afternoon, I think. I usually go in the afternoon. Markets in that region are always laid out in rings.
Was anyone with you?
My sister was with me — no, wait, that was a different trip. I remember my chest going tight.
Roughly how long were you looking for the way out?
I don't know how long it took. Honestly I couldn't tell you.
